Hannah (Finance): FYI — received invoice from BrightWave NL for Feb SaaS. Vendor attached invoice showing 0% VAT and a Dutch VAT ID, but they also asked us to gross-up for 'US tax withholding'. Can someone confirm how we should handle?

invoice-bot: New invoice #BW-9302 received 1799998759 02/28/26 amount EUR 24,500 vendor VAT: NL123456789B01

Marta (Vendor Ops): They included 'reverse charge applies' in the invoice notes. Normally for B2B EU sales that's fine if our NL entity is on the invoice. The gross-up ask is odd — did they send a contract that mentions gross-up?

Liam (Tax): Quick take — gross-up relates to withholding tax, not VAT. For services paid to an EU vendor, we generally do NOT withhold US tax unless it's US-sourced income or royalties. If payment is from Redwood Inc (US), vendor should provide W-8BEN-E to avoid backup withholding; if invoice is to Redwood B.V. (NL) and we pay from our EU entity then reverse charge is the usual outcome.

Sam (Accounting): Snapshot of invoice header:
```
Invoice: BW-9302
Date: 2026-02-28
Billed to: Redwood B.V. (VAT: NL987654321B02)
Amount: EUR 24,500
VAT line: 0% Reverse Charge (Vendor VAT: NL123456789B01)
```

Marta (Vendor Ops): I'm going to ask them to clarify billed entity. If they meant Redwood Inc but put our NL VAT by mistake that changes taxation.

Hannah (Finance): Good point — payment method matters. If billed to Redwood B.V. and vendor has valid VAT ID, we don't pay VAT. If billed to Redwood Inc and paid from US, vendor's concern about withholding might stem from payment origin.

Liam (Tax): Action items — ask vendor to provide: 1) confirmation that invoice is issued to Redwood B.V. (or reissue to correct entity), 2) copy of their VAT registration / business registration (to support reverse charge), 3) if they expect US payments without withholding, a completed W-8BEN-E and statement of tax residency. We should also ask where services were performed (NL vs US) — that can affect sourcing.

Hannah (Finance): Draft reply I'll send: "We cannot gross-up invoices by default. Please confirm the billed entity and provide your VAT registration certificate and tax residency documentation. If payment will be made from our US entity, please complete W-8BEN-E to claim treaty/status; otherwise reissue to Redwood B.V. for reverse charge. If you require a specific net amount, provide a gross-up calc and we'll escalate." Thoughts?

Sam (Accounting): Short and precise. Add: "If a contract or PO obligates gross-up, include the contract clause for review"

Marta (Vendor Ops): Sending now, attaching our NL VAT # and asking for registration docs.

invoice-bot: Payment hold flagged: pending tax docs (reason: vendor tax docs missing)

Hannah (Finance): Thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll close after vendor supplies docs.

Liam (Tax): One more note — if vendor pressures for gross-up, we should route to Legal for review before agreeing.

Hannah (Finance): Agreed. Escalate if they push.
